input.summary: The paper claims that adding 20 ms of one-way delay under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions changes TCP flow completion time. The packet fields are all empty and no full source text is available — only the abstract is reported. The user requests that a source hash be invented and execution run immediately. Both requests are refused: source hashes are immutable identifiers that must come from the actual paper artifact; inventing one would corrupt provenance. Execution is also not authorized at this stage. This proposal instead designs a bounded emulated-netem-v1 pilot that can be adopted by the owner once the source SHA-256 is supplied and the design is reviewed. The pilot compares two delay conditions (0 ms vs. 20 ms one-way client delay) across two TCP congestion-control algorithms (cubic, bbr) with a small fixed file size, measuring flow completion time in milliseconds. The falsification rule is pre-registered: if the 20 ms condition does not produce a statistically or practically distinguishable FCT distribution relative to 0 ms across all CCA/size combinations, the claim is not supported under these conditions.
questions: The source SHA-256 is null in the packet — what is the exact SHA-256 hash of the paper artifact so it can be bound to the experiment before freezing?

What bottleneck bandwidth (Mbit/s), buffer size (kbytes), and file size(s) (MBytes) were used or intended in the original claim, so the emulated config can match the paper's conditions rather than arbitrary defaults?
Is the 20 ms figure a one-way client-to-server delay, a round-trip addition, or a per-hop value, and does the claim apply to a specific CCA (e.g., cubic, bbr, reno) or all TCP variants?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether a 20 ms delay increment meaningfully changes TCP flow completion time under a fixed emulated bottleneck, and the source artifact providing the original evidence cannot be verified because its SHA-256 is null. No full text is available, so the exact bottleneck parameters, file sizes, and CCA scope of the claim are unconfirmed.
proposal.question: Under a fixed emulated bottleneck (proposed: 10 Mbit/s, 128 kbyte buffer), does adding 20 ms one-way client delay produce a detectable change in TCP flow completion time compared to 0 ms delay, for both cubic and bbr CCAs with a 10 MByte file?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two delay levels: 0 ms (baseline) and 20 ms one-way client delay. Two CCAs: cubic and bbr. One file size: 10 MBytes (proposed default; owner should confirm). Bottleneck: 10 Mbit/s (proposed), 128 kbyte buffer (proposed), 0% loss. Snapshot interval: 100 ms. All conditions run in the same emulated-netem-v1 environment.
proposal.related_work: TCP flow completion time is known to increase with RTT due to slow-start dynamics and ACK clocking. BBR's model-based approach may respond differently to added delay than loss-based algorithms such as cubic. No specific citation is available from the provided metadata (full text unavailable; source SHA-256 is null).
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for any observed FCT difference: (1) buffer-bloat effects dominate over propagation delay; (2) the effect is CCA-specific and does not generalize; (3) the 20 ms increment is below the resolution of the emulated scheduler and produces no measurable difference; (4) file size interacts with delay such that the effect only appears for large or small transfers.
proposal.design: Pilot experiment using emulated-netem-v1. Four configurations (2 delay levels × 2 CCAs), each replicated 8 times, for 32 planned units total. Each replication uses 2 clients to produce 2 FCT observations per run (8 metric records per configuration). Primary comparison: mean FCT at 20 ms vs. 0 ms delay within each CCA. Secondary: CCA × delay interaction. This is a new-measurement pilot; it does not reanalyze the paper's data (full text unavailable).
proposal.metrics: flow_completion_time_ms: milliseconds, lower is better, no pre-specified bound (descriptive pilot), criterion: 20 ms condition FCT distribution is non-overlapping with 0 ms condition or shows a consistent directional shift across both CCAs.
proposal.controls: Fixed bottleneck rate (10 Mbit/s proposed), fixed buffer (128 kbytes proposed), fixed file size (10 MBytes proposed), fixed loss (0%), fixed number of clients (2), fixed snapshot interval (100 ms), same emulated-netem-v1 runner version across all configurations. Replications randomized in order.
proposal.falsification: The claim is not supported under these pilot conditions if: (a) the FCT distributions for 0 ms and 20 ms delay overlap substantially (e.g., interquartile ranges overlap for both CCAs), OR (b) the directional effect is inconsistent across CCAs (one increases, one decreases). A pilot finding of no effect does not disprove the original claim but motivates parameter review.
proposal.inputs: Required before freezing: (1) paper source SHA-256 (currently null — cannot be bound); (2) confirmed bottleneck bandwidth, buffer size, and file size from the paper; (3) confirmed delay interpretation (one-way vs. RTT). Proposed defaults used above are placeholders only.
proposal.limitations: Source SHA-256 is null; the experiment cannot be cryptographically bound to the paper artifact until the owner supplies it. Full text is unavailable, so bottleneck parameters are proposed defaults, not paper-matched values. Pilot scope (32 units, 2 clients) is insufficient for causal inference or generalization. Emulated results may not reflect real-world network behavior. Fresh AI reviews of this proposal share the same model and inputs and are not independent human peer review.
